subject: Request: safeguard pricing authorization for HearthWell pilot
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: safeguard pricing authorization for HearthWell pilot

Team —

Quick background: HearthWell (digital care provider) is ready to sign a 12-month dedicated-capacity pilot that will convert to a multi-year commitment if they hit usage thresholds. Commercially, they want a one-time "safeguard" (loss-avoidance) discount of 45% on hosted inference for the first 3 months to offset migration risk and integration costs. Net-new ARR at conversion looks reasonable (~$540k run rate) but the upfront ramp will be light for 30–60 days.

Why I'm asking: this request exceeds my threshold for AE-level discounts. Because the ask materially impacts unit economics in the pilot period, I need VP/CFO clearance for a non-standard safety-net concession tied to firm conversion language.

What I recommend:
- Approve a 40% safeguard discount for months 0–3 conditioned on a signed MOU that guarantees a 12-month reserved commitment if usage enters the conversion tier by month 4.
- Add a step-down: month 4–6 at 20% discount to soften revenue cliff.
- Include a clawback: if customer cancels before month 12, credits are prorated and recovered against their remaining invoice schedule.

Expected impact: with the recommended structure we preserve a path to full-rate economics by month 4 while giving the customer a low-friction onboarding window. I attached the MOA "HearthWell_MA_plan.pdf" and a draft commercial summary in Drive.

Ask: Marissa/Markus — can you review overnight? Jordan, can you pull together the estimated revenue/margin delta for the first 6 months (high/med/low ramp scenarios)? Need a yes/no + conditions so I can present to the customer tomorrow.

Thanks,

Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
chloe_martin@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192

Attachment: HearthWell_MA_plan.pdf (pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: safeguard pricing authorization for HearthWell pilot

Chloe —

Thanks for the concise note and the MOA. I support the approach in principle but need a tighter financial readout before I can clear anything to the CFO. Specifically:

1) Delta to gross margin and EBITDA for the first 6 months (three ramp scenarios).
2) A clear conversion trigger (metrics + timeline) and contract language for the clawback.
3) Confirmation that the reserved capacity can be reduced in month 2 if usage is below the low-ramp threshold (operationally acceptable).

Jordan — can you provide the three scenarios by EOD today? Use the template from the "pricing-impact" sheet in the finance folder.

Markus — if the numbers look like the middle scenario (break-even by month 4), I think we can present a consolidated ask to CFO for a limited, time-boxed authorization. If it's the low scenario, we should consider a smaller initial discount + higher onboarding credits instead.

Marissa Cole
CFO (acting) — Finance & Commercial Ops
marissa_cole@redwood.com

All —

Attached the modeled scenarios (proposed_pricing_table.xlsx). Summary below:

High ramp (best case)
- Conversion to full commitment by month 3.
- 40% reduction in GAAP revenue for months 0–3, offset by faster ARR scale.
- Net unit cost recovered by month 4.

Mid ramp (probable)
- Conversion by month 4–5.
- Net present value impact ~ -6% over first 12 months vs standard pricing.

Low ramp (conservative)
- No conversion within 6 months.
- NPV impact materially higher — recommends 25% initial discount + 3 months onboarding credits instead of 40% safeguard.

Recommendations (commercial):
1) Approve the 40% safeguard for months 0–3 but only if we add a minimum commitment language and a 20% step-down for months 4–6.
2) Add an onboarding service credit (50k engineering hours/$) that is non-refundable and applied to integration work — reduces cash exposure.
3) Include a renew/convert clause: if customer reaches X API tokens/day for 14 consecutive days between month 3–6, automatic conversion to the reserved rate is triggered.

I've also included a short negotiation playbook for the AE to present to the customer so we don't accept counter-offers that trade away long-term economics.

Jordan Blake
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com

Attachment: proposed_pricing_table.xlsx

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 16:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: safeguard pricing authorization for HearthWell pilot

Chloe/Jordan —

Read the attachment and Jordan's scenarios. I'm comfortable authorizing a conditional approval to proceed with the 40% safeguard for months 0–3 with the following conditions:

1) Legal to include the conversion trigger and the clawback language in the MOU. No open-ended credits.
2) Onboarding service credit must be applied to SOW and capped at $50k (as Jordan suggested).
3) Finance to sign off on the mid-scenario economics (Marissa — if you confirm mid scenario, this stands).
4) Sales must secure a signed MOU with the conversion commitment by start of month 3 or the discount expires.

If Marissa confirms mid scenario numbers by EOD tomorrow, I'll mark this as VP-level authorization and route to CFO for final signature. Chloe — you have clearance to present this structured offer to Danielle, emphasize the conversion trigger and the limited-time nature of the safeguard.

-Markus

Markus Klein
VP, Commercial Strategy
markus_klein@redwood.com
